original_card.question: Can one misleading historical-current claim or missing research cross-reference be corrected?
methods: Trace one confusing path from onboarding to its authoritative source.
Index one tightly related family of obstructions with explicit excluded and open hypotheses.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Produce evidence-backed navigation, preserve historical records and avoid a duplicate global survey.

first_step.inspect: Follow one link from the selected record to its review and compare a potentially stale historical claim.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Repair one confusing path or produce a scoped map of one related obstruction family.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Clear navigation lowers entry cost for central research; a global survey without a concrete fix is not required.
allowed_variations: One historical-current ambiguity or one bounded family index.
scope_change_triggers: Rewriting frozen scientific packages just to change their historical wording.

actual_scope: For the T74 line (15 open conditional-kappa PRs plus the PR2265 baseline): pin each claimed kappa; transcribe and re-check the stated numbers between pinned PRs in PR bodies and pinned READMEs; parse and check the predecessor gates in every pinned verify_release.py; map which claims have independent checks.
scope_change_reason: Drawn on the consolidation track (seed 99); the concrete misleading claims are inter-PR comparison statements on the busiest open line, so the card is narrowed to that ledger.
bottleneck_link: Reviewers of the busiest open claim line need a correct pinned ordering, to know whether the stated comparisons (and the release gates behind them) are right, and an honest list of what is independently verified.
stop_rule: Stop after the pinned ledger, the statement check (asserted flagged set, controls), the gate check and the independent-check map; two adversarial review rounds folded in.
evidence: ledger.py: 16 pinned claim files; 95 statements (32 body, 63 README), 84 consistent (2 ambiguous 2269/2281 quotes), 11 flagged: wrong-target differences (PR2302; PR2374 body+README; PR2435 body+README), self-kappa quoted as predecessor's in READMEs of PR2435/PR2447/PR2474, stale 'about 1.28e-5' boilerplate in PR2288/PR2302/PR2312 READMEs; 82 release gates attributed to pinned PRs (55 exact, 17 conservative, 10 PR2265 43-digit truncation 9.7e-45 below) all pass, so no kappa or gate is affected; one gate label slip (PR2363 gate reports PR2322) in 5 scripts; 315/315 negative and 11/11 positive controls; --live drift 0 at snapshot.
author: Sagar Thakrar
ai_assistance: Prepared with substantial AI assistance: Claude Code (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5) wrote the ledger script and text. No independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Are the owner fills of PR2436, PR2462 and PR2474 exactly optimal for their words, and do the words recount to their reports?
open_questions.why_it_matters: These are the top three T74 claims and have no independent check.
open_questions.first_step: Run PR2442's owner_optimum.py and PR2446/PR2466's checker on the pinned files.
open_questions.blocked_by: The words and owner maps must be pinned and adapted to the checker.

open_questions.question: Can each claim file record its predecessors as (PR, exact kappa) so this ledger becomes automatic?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The release gates already hold these values; the text errors found here come from hand-written comparison sentences.
open_questions.first_step: Propose an optional 'predecessors' field for OUTER-CLAIM.json in the package guide.
open_questions.blocked_by: Maintainer agreement on the claim-file schema.
